_about: Swarm at the pause, 2026-11-13. Src codes: B = critic/board.md; toP/toC/toPa/toS = critic/to-<line>.md; P/, C/, Pa/, S/ = probability/, counting/, path/, source/ under research/theory/swarm/; r1 = reply/report round 1. Tags: claimed (in claims.md, critic not yet looked), confirmed-by-critic (re-derived, recomputed, or where noted only read), refuted, open (guessed or unproved). In results, label = short name, line = plain statement.

problem.label: The problem
problem.line: Why does trapped chaos live exponentially longer as a face grows, and what sets the rate?
problem.statement: A face of A cells on gump's hull dies after a memoryless wait whose log grows about 0.21-0.22 per cell (2D cousin: 0.36-0.42). Why exponential in area, and what sets the rate gamma?
problem.what_counts: Best: a theorem for gump or the 2D rule (or why not); then a close relative with a theorem; a theorem under one testable hypothesis; a formula for gamma fitting both ranges; side facts, especially symmetry.
problem.src: PROBLEM.md, The problem; What would count

results.label: Cells independent given the row

results.label: Theorem A near the anchor

results.label: One-step comparison is dead

results.label: Block comparisons need fast seeding

results.label: Lemma 3: certificate gives lifetime

results.label: Trapdoor bounds
results.line: Bounds on how soon a measure-preserving map falls into a trapdoor.

results.label: Reversible cousin never dies
results.line: A reversible relative of gump keeps its faces alive forever: no route there.

results.label: Early death exactly exponential
results.line: From random soup, chance the 2D edge is empty at age k falls exactly exponentially in length.

results.label: Exact early rates
results.line: Per-cell rates at ages 1 and 2: 0.551535 and 0.467693.

results.label: Walls and mirrors at fixed age

results.label: Cube decomposition beneath a face
results.line: Cells beneath a gump face split into cubes; one-step death decided cube by cube.

results.label: Lone-cube guard
results.line: A lone live cube keeps a slab face alive for k generations.

results.label: Gaps persist
results.line: A long empty stretch keeps its middle empty for a while.

results.label: Early rate depends on the soup
results.line: The early-age rate depends on starting density, so it is not the long-run exponent.

results.label: At fixed age, rule = dice
results.line: Up to a fixed age the true rule equals a dice model with enough rows.

results.label: A live cell thins beneath
results.line: A live edge cell makes the cells beneath slightly less likely alive.

results.label: Rim lemma
results.line: A dead patch refills only from its edge, one cell per generation at most.

results.label: Theorem P
results.line: A one-step inequality for any face statistic bounds the death rate, no memory assumed.

results.label: Theorem P-bar, pooled form
results.line: Deaths = entries into a low set times a committor of the pooled one-step table.

results.label: Losses are sealed-set extinctions

results.label: Sealed sets characterised
results.line: Sealed sets are complements of bootstrap-closed sets; their top layer is rigid.

results.label: Caricature with exact area law
results.line: In biased voter dynamics a droplet's death chance is exactly exponential in size.

results.label: Sealed facts don't imply law

results.label: Dying faces shrink, not flash

results.label: Exact deterministic dice source
results.line: A suitable deterministic bulk feeds the top layers perfectly fair coins, even with feedback.

results.label: Random rules are deterministic tops
results.line: Any random automaton with rational odds is the top of a deterministic one.

results.label: Markovian projection

results.label: Threshold bulk is no source
results.line: A bulk without overcrowding makes no lasting randomness.

results.label: Frozen drive cells

joint_picture.formula_for_gamma: None. Path's guess Th gives about 0.21 'from eight numbers and a ruler', near gump's 0.21-0.22; nothing for 2D's 0.36-0.42.
joint_picture.theorems: Exponential lifetime is proved only for dice or deterministic relatives near the 'equal cells by a fair coin' anchor, modulo F1, F2; no lower bound for gump or the 2D rule.
joint_picture.limits: Area law holds in hulls and thick slabs only; wide thin slabs die by bands (0.12 vs 0.21 per cell) (E12).

library.label: The library shelf

key_sources.result: 1D finite contact process: log lifetime linear in N; upper bound by monotonicity, lower by duality.
d>=2: lifetime/mean is exponential; 'fast regeneration implies memoryless'.
log mean extinction time / volume converges.
Shortest proof of exponential extinction: coupling, supermultiplicativity.
Comparison with oriented percolation, without monotonicity.
Ratio mixing implies exponential hitting time of rare sets.
Conditionally invariant measures; none in a finite deterministic system.
Stable chaos: size-exponential transients, numerical only.
